text: What is the smallest number that must be added to 1,234 to make it divisible by 9?
explanation: A number is divisible by 9 when its digit sum is. Here 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10, and the next multiple of 9 above 10 is 18 — so the digit sum must gain 8, and adding 8 gives 1,242 with digit sum 9. (Check directly: 1,234 = 9 x 137 + 1, so 8 more reaches 9 x 138.) Adding 2 to reach a digit sum of 12 is the trap: 12 is a multiple of 3, not of 9.

text: What is the unit digit of 7 raised to the power 63?
explanation: The unit digits of powers of 7 cycle 7, 9, 3, 1 with period 4. Since 63 = 4 x 15 + 3, the answer is the third in the cycle, 3.

text: The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their LCM is 180. If one number is 36, what is the other?
explanation: For two numbers, HCF x LCM = product. So the other number is (12 x 180)/36 = 60. (Check: HCF(36, 60) = 12 and LCM = 180.)

text: How many numbers from 1 to 200 are divisible by 3 or by 5?
explanation: Divisible by 3: 66. By 5: 40. By both, that is by 15: 13. So 66 + 40 - 13 = 93. Adding without removing the overlap gives 106 and counts every multiple of 15 twice.

text: What is the simple interest on Rs 24,000 at 7.5% a year for 2 years?
explanation: Simple interest is P x R x T/100 = 24,000 x 7.5 x 2/100 = 3,600. The Rs 3,735 option is the COMPOUND interest for the same two years, which is larger because the first year's interest earns in the second.

text: A sum doubles in 8 years under simple interest. In how many years does it become five times itself at the same rate?
explanation: Doubling means the interest equals the principal in 8 years, so each 'principal' of interest takes 8 years. Five times needs four principals of interest: 4 x 8 = 32 years. (The rate is 12.5% a year, which is not needed.)

text: What is the compound interest on Rs 10,000 at 10% a year for 2 years, compounded annually?
explanation: After one year 11,000; after two, 11,000 x 1.1 = 12,100. The interest is 2,100. Simple interest would be 2,000, and the extra Rs 100 is the 10% earned in year two on year one's Rs 1,000 of interest.

text: The difference between the compound and simple interest on a sum for 2 years at 10% a year is Rs 150. What is the sum?
explanation: For two years the gap is the interest earned on the first year's interest: P x (10/100) x (10/100) = P/100. So P/100 = 150 and P = 15,000. The general form is P x (R/100) squared for two years.

text: A father is three times as old as his son. In 12 years he will be twice as old. How old is the son now?
explanation: Let the son be s, so the father is 3s. In 12 years 3s + 12 = 2(s + 12), giving s = 12. (Check: 12 and 36 now; 24 and 48 in twelve years.)

text: The ratio of two sisters' ages is 5:3 and the difference is 8 years. What will the ratio be in 8 years?
explanation: The difference of 2 parts is 8 years, so a part is 4 and the ages are 20 and 12. In eight years they are 28 and 20, which is 7:5. An age DIFFERENCE never changes, which is the fact most of these questions turn on.

text: If 1 March 2027 is a Monday, what day is 1 April 2027?
explanation: March has 31 days, and 31 = 4 x 7 + 3, so 1 April falls three weekdays after Monday: Thursday. Only the remainder matters — the whole weeks pass unnoticed.

text: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 3:40?
explanation: The minute hand is at 40 x 6 = 240 degrees from twelve. The hour hand is at 3 x 30 plus 40 x 0.5 = 90 + 20 = 110 degrees. The gap is 240 - 110 = 130 degrees. Leaving the hour hand at 90 gives 150 and forgets that it creeps forward as the minutes pass.

text: A rectangular hall is 24 m by 15 m. How many square tiles of side 60 cm are needed to cover the floor?
explanation: The floor is 360 square metres. Each tile is 0.6 x 0.6 = 0.36 square metres, so 360/0.36 = 1,000 tiles. Mixing metres and centimetres is the whole difficulty here — convert once, at the start.

text: If the radius of a circle is increased by 20%, by what percentage does its area increase?
explanation: Area goes as the square of the radius: 1.2 squared = 1.44, a rise of 44%. A length scales by 1.2 and an area by 1.44 — the answer 20% confuses the two, and 40% doubles the percentage instead of squaring the factor.

text: Placements in one department, by year. 2023: 120 offers from 150 students. 2024: 144 offers from 180 students. 2025: 189 offers from 210 students. In which year was the offer rate highest?
explanation: The rates are 120/150 = 80%, 144/180 = 80% and 189/210 = 90%. 2025 is highest. The count of offers rose every year, so reading the biggest number rather than the rate gets the right answer here by luck — which is why the next question changes that.

text: Placements in one department, by year. 2023: 120 offers from 150 students. 2024: 144 offers from 180 students. 2025: 189 offers from 210 students. In which year did the offer RATE fall compared with the year before, if any?
explanation: The rates are 80%, 80% and 90%: 2024 held steady and 2025 improved, so the rate fell in none of them. 'Held steady' is not 'fell', and the offer count rising is not the same thing as the rate rising — in 2024 the count rose by 24 while the rate did not move at all.

text: A mock test has four sections. Verbal: 18 correct of 25. Reasoning: 21 of 25. Numerical: 24 of 40. Coding: 7 of 10. In which section was the candidate weakest as a proportion of the marks available?
explanation: The proportions are 72%, 84%, 60% and 70%. Numerical is lowest at 60%, even though it is where the candidate got the MOST answers right (24). Comparing raw counts across sections of different lengths is the mistake this question is built on.

text: A mock test has four sections. Verbal: 18 correct of 25. Reasoning: 21 of 25. Numerical: 24 of 40. Coding: 7 of 10. Each correct answer is worth 1 mark and each wrong answer loses 0.25. Assuming every question was attempted, what is the total score?
explanation: Correct answers: 18 + 21 + 24 + 7 = 70. Wrong answers: 7 + 4 + 16 + 3 = 30, costing 30 x 0.25 = 7.5. The score is 70 - 7.5 = 62.5. Forgetting the penalty gives 70, which is why reading the mark scheme is part of the question.
